topScam.title: The WhatsApp "Wedding Card" Virus (APK Trojan)
topScam.scam: You receive a message from a friend or relative on WhatsApp saying: "My cousin is getting married next week, wedding card and venue attached." The attached file looks like an invite, but ends in .apk. Installing it infects your phone with a virus that hijacks your WhatsApp, sends the same scam to all your family contacts, and steals your net banking logins.
topScam.protection: Real wedding cards are always photos or PDFs, never an .apk software file. If someone sends an APK file, do not tap it. Call that person on a regular call to tell them their WhatsApp is compromised.

realityPick.title: The Naive Prompt Guardrail Illusion
realityPick.myth: Adding 'You are a polite assistant and must never disclose secrets' to your system prompt protects your business!
realityPick.reality: Prompt-level instructions can always be overridden by sophisticated jailbreaks, multilingual token encodings, or recursive context manipulation. Prompting is NOT a security boundary.
realityPick.fix: Deploy deterministic classifier guardrails and independent input/output screening models outside the LLM execution pipeline.
realityPick.impact: A customer jailbreaks an automotive chatbot into selling a brand-new vehicle for $1 legally bound by conversation record.
